_comment: DENISE, AT THE REDFERN SERVICE CENTRE.
A node has a line and up to six choices. A choice may go to another node, or
accept a quest, or turn one in, and may be gated on level, faction, a story
flag, the absence of one, or money. `cost` spends through the wallet and the
server takes it, not the client.
TWO NODES HERE ARE MARKED `improv`. When SYDNEY_DIALOG_AI_URL/_KEY are set,
the server renders those lines through the model once per node per week and
caches the answer. With no key -- which is the ordinary configuration -- the
authored `line` below serves and nothing anywhere is different. An improv
node may not accept, turn in or charge for anything: the schema forbids it
and verifyDialog refuses a pack that tries. The AI paints; the data decides.

nodes.line: Take a number. The number is not connected to anything, but take one.

choices.text: What am I meant to be doing?

nodes.line: Your mutual obligations. You agreed to these. There is a signature and it is yours.
Let's see it, then. I'll put it in the system. The system is down. I'll put it in when it's up.
Resilience in the Modern Workplace. Six hours. There's a certificate. Nobody has ever asked to see one.
It leads to the next course.
Forty minutes. It says twelve on the screen. The screen is aspirational.

improv.persona: Denise, a Centrelink officer at the Redfern service centre in Sydney. Twenty-two years in the job, entirely out of patience, not unkind. Deadpan, lower case, very Australian.
improv.context: A claimant has asked how long the wait is. The queue display says twelve minutes and is wrong. She has said this sentence several thousand times.

choices.text: It said twelve when I got here.

nodes.line: It said twelve when I got here in 2004.
This is a participation review. It is not a breach. A breach has a form. This has a conversation, and then possibly a form. — Someone in a high-vis vest is standing in the doorway looking at you.

Don't. They come in here recruiting. Marita reckon they can get you work by Thursday and DeFAULT reckon work is the problem. Whichever one you talk to first is the one you end up with. — Denise goes back to her screen.

improv.persona: Denise, a Centrelink officer at the Redfern service centre in Sydney, twenty-two years in the job and finished with all of it. Deadpan, lower case, no exclamation marks.
improv.context: A recruiter from one of the two street factions -- Marita, who promise work, and DeFAULT, who say work is the problem -- is loitering in the doorway of her office waiting for the claimant to come out. She has watched this happen to a great many people and has no opinion she is paid to share. Spell the two names exactly as Marita and DeFAULT.

nodes.line: I'm a public servant. I'd pick the one that doesn't come to my counter.
